macro.reasoning: Temperature shows a clear downward trend from ~33°C in mid-May to ~31.9°C by July 1, with recent values oscillating 30-32°C. The last 10 days average 30.5°C. Humidity is rising (57% to 65%) and precipitation increasing, both associated with cooling. A gradual decline of ~0.2-0.3°C/day continues the observed late-June trend into early July.

micro.reasoning: Temperature shows a gradual cooling trend from late June into early July, with recent values oscillating around 31-32°C. The last 7 days show a slight downward drift (31.9 → 31.4 → 30.2 → 31.4 → 31.9), but the broader pattern since mid-June indicates a slow decline from the 33-34°C range. Humidity remains moderate (57-65%) with intermittent rain, supporting continued mild cooling. Forecast projects a steady 0.2-0.3°C daily decrease.
step_reasoning: Day 1: Recent cooling momentum continues; last value 31.9°C with rain and moderate humidity suggests slight drop to ~31.5°C
Day 2: Persistent cloud cover and humidity around 60% limit daytime heating; trend supports further decline to ~31.2°C
Day 3: No strong warming catalysts; seasonal progression into July favors gradual cooling to ~31.0°C
Day 4: Stable pattern of mild days and humid nights sustains slow downward drift to ~30.8°C
Day 5: Continued absence of heatwave signals; model consistency points to ~30.5°C
Day 6: Long-term trend from mid-June (34°C → 32°C) extrapolates to ~30.3°C
Day 7: Equilibrium near 30°C expected as summer stabilizes; final forecast ~30.0°C

synthesis.reasoning: Both macro and micro forecasts converge on an identical 7-day cooling trajectory (31.5→30.0°C), reflecting strong consensus. The macro model emphasizes the sustained late-June downtrend (33→31.9°C over 6 weeks), rising humidity (57→65%), and increasing precipitation as physical drivers. The micro model adds granular daily reasoning: recent oscillation (31.9→31.4→30.2→31.4→31.9) masks a persistent 0.2-0.3°C/day drift, with no heatwave catalysts present. Weighting is effectively 50/50 given identical outputs; uncertainty is low (±0.5°C) due to model agreement and consistent covariates (humidity, rain, wind).
